sense: a chance or means to do something

terms.grammar: noun, third declension; with the genitive of a gerund, or ut
evidence: Cic. Mil. 45: Milōnī manendī nūlla facultās
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “capability, possibility, power, means, opportunity”. For “it is possible that …” see possible: fierī potest ut.

terms.gloss: the chance, the opportunity (to do something)
evidence: Cic. Fam. 10.13.1: ut prīmum potestās data est
terms.comment: Potestātem facere, to give someone the chance (Cic. Cat. 3.11, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Milōnī manendī nūlla facultās, exeundī nōn causa sōlum sed etiam necessitās fuit
phrases.english: Milo had no possibility of staying, and for setting out not only a reason but a necessity

phrases.latin: ut prīmum potestās data est augendae dignitātis tuae, nihil praetermīsī in tē ōrnandō
phrases.english: as soon as I had the chance to add to your standing, I left nothing undone to honour you

phrases.latin: proptereā quod reliquīs tamen fugae facultās darētur
phrases.english: because the rest, at least, had the possibility of flight

sources: Lewis & Short: facultas · Lewis & Short: potestas · Lewis & Short: occasio
Cicero (Mil. 38, 45; Fam. 10.13.1) and Caesar (BG 1.32.5) checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
